entity.title: Entity
entity.description: An object with a unique identity and lifecycle. The unit of organization in the SteerSpec rule system.

rules.body: IS an object that has a unique identity that persists over time.
MAY transition through multiple states during its lifecycle.
MAY possess one or more properties.
The behavior of an entity IS defined entirely by the Rules applicable to its identity, properties, and states.
HAS an Entity Unique Identifier.
MAY inherit the rule set of exactly one other Entity, declared in an `inherits` field holding the parent's Entity Unique Identifier.
An `inherits` reference to an Entity outside the referencing Entity's Realm tree MUST use the qualified form `<realm-id>:<EUID>`, naming a declared dependency or one of its sub-realms.
An inheritance chain MUST NOT contain cycles or exceed three hops.

An inheriting Entity MUST acquire the parent's effective rule set, the parent's own Published and Implemented Rules together with those the parent inherits, as read-only references that remain owned by their original Entity.
An inheriting Entity's Rule Set MUST cover only the Rules it owns.
MAY declare a `visibility` of `private`, `protected` or `public`; when it is absent, a sub-entity takes the visibility of the Entity containing it and any other Entity is `public`.
Visibility `public` IS permission to inherit the Entity and to override its Rules from any Realm.
Visibility `protected` IS permission to inherit the Entity from any Realm and to override its Rules only from within its Realm tree.

Visibility `private` IS permission to inherit the Entity only from within its Realm tree and to override its Rules only from the Realm holding it, not from a parent, child or sibling sub-realm of that Realm.

The visibility of an Entity MUST NOT be wider than that of the Entity it inherits and MUST NOT be wider than that of the Entity containing it, where `private` is narrower than `protected` and `protected` is narrower than `public`.

An `inherits` declaration MUST be permitted by the visibility of the inherited Entity, and an `overrides` declaration on a Rule that is not Abandoned, Retired or Terminated MUST be permitted by the visibility of every Entity from the inherited Entity up to and including the owner of the overridden Rule, each measured from the Realm of the declaring Entity and applied as if that Entity owned the Rule.
MAY declare a `standards` array of Standard References in its `entity` object.

entity.title: Entity Unique Identifier
entity.description: The unique identifier assigned to each entity within a Realm.

rules.body: MUST have a length of at least 3 and at most 18 characters.
IS a string of letters or numbers only.
IS unique within the Realm.

notes.content: Inheritance is specialisation, not containment: parent (sub-entities) nests an Entity inside another, inherits lets an Entity reuse another Entity's rule set without copying it, in the same Realm or across a declared dependency. Inherited Rules stay owned by the parent (ENT-009). A cross-realm parent is frozen at the dependency version pinned in realm.json, so its changes arrive only on a dependency bump; a same-realm parent is not pinned, and child and parent evolve together within their Realm's version. Only Published and Implemented parent Rules are inherited; Draft text may still change and Abandoned, Retired or Terminated Rules are not in force. A parent's sub-entities are not inherited.

Visibility is applied along the chain because an Entity's own visibility would otherwise be bypassed. Take a `public` Entity A with a Rule R, a `protected` Entity B that inherits A, and an Entity D in an unrelated Realm that inherits B. D may inherit B, but it cannot override R, even though A alone would allow it: B's visibility applies to R as if B owned it, although R remains owned by A (ENT-009). The check stops at the owner, since Entities above it have no say over that Rule. An `inherits` is checked against the inherited Entity alone, because ENT-015 keeps that Entity no wider than those above it. An `overrides` is checked whatever the state of the Rule it names. A superseded Rule stays in force until it is Retired, so the state exemption here and in NTE-012 does not cover it.
